sources.entry: C / Python: _Build your own VPN/Virtual Switch_

summary.one_liner: A teaching project that builds a layer-2 virtual switch (VSwitch in Python) and client ports (VPort in C) that bridge Ethernet frames over UDP so computers across the Internet appear to share one LAN.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a server program, vswitch.py, that simulates a physical Ethernet switch by keeping a MAC address table and forwarding frames to the correct port. Each client runs vport.c, which attaches to a Linux TAP virtual network device and relays frames between the local kernel and the VSwitch over a UDP socket. Frames the switch does not have a table entry for are flooded to all other ports so the destination can answer and be learned. The result is that machines on different networks can ping each other on a shared 10.1.1.0/24 subnet. The README states the design only at a high level and does not describe encryption, authentication, or NAT traversal.
use_cases: learn how a layer-2 network switch forwards frames
connect computers over the Internet into one virtual LAN
understand TAP devices and virtual network interfaces
build a simple VPN-like overlay for testing
study a ZeroTier-style virtual switch implementation
how_to_run: python3 vswitch.py ${SERVER_PORT}  (on a server with a public IP)
sudo ip addr add 10.1.1.101/24 dev tapyuan && sudo ip link set tapyuan up  (client 1 TAP setup)
sudo ip addr add 10.1.1.102/24 dev tapyuan && sudo ip link set tapyuan up  (client 2 TAP setup)
ping 10.1.1.102 from client 1 to test connectivity
notable: Implements a layer-2 MAC-learning switch with flooding for unknown destinations
Uses a Linux TAP device so the OS sees a normal network interface
Architecture diagram showing VSwitch, VPort, and TAP/UDP relay path
Part of the codecrafters build-your-own-x list under network stack projects
caveats: Requires Linux and root privileges (sudo) to create and configure TAP devices
README is a short project guide; no license, security, or production-readiness information is given
Deployment needs a server with a public IP and at least two clients
keywords: share a network across the internet
connect computers over internet as lan
